title: Lincoln Road purchase and heritage designations
subtitle: US tariff response motion, parking reductions for affordable housing, Wideman Road speed limit, and active transportation grant.
overview: Council approved $2,900,000 in capital funding to acquire 250 Lincoln Road, the former church site, as part of its affordable housing work. The building can be used for up to 3 years as City programming space for public art organizations and other City programs {{vote:m10}}. Council also directed notices of intention to designate five properties under the Ontario Heritage Act and asked staff to review financial incentives for designated heritage properties {{vote:m11}}.

Other approvals: parking reduction guidelines meant to speed up affordable housing projects {{vote:m7}}, a lower speed limit of 50 km/h on part of Wideman Road {{vote:m5}}, and a federal Active Transportation Fund application with an $800,000 City share {{vote:m9}}. Council received the 2024 drinking water reports {{vote:m6}}.

Council also passed a motion on proposed US tariffs. It calls on other governments to act and asks staff to look at limiting the impact on City services and at buying more from Canadian sources {{vote:m12}}. Council met in closed session on legal advice, litigation and land matters. The minutes report no public outcome from it.

decisions.detail: Council approved $2,900,000 in capital funding for the purchase, improvements, costs and future demolition, and temporary City programming use of the facility for up to 3 years.

Council directed the Clerk to issue notices of intention to designate 33 Allen Street East, 75 Allen Street East, 35 Alexandra Avenue, 12 Bridgeport Road East and 39 Dupont Street East, and directed staff to review financial incentives for heritage properties.
Council stands with Team Canada against tariffs, asks other governments and the economic development agency to act, and directs staff to review procurement and limit the impact on City services.
Council approved guidelines that set out when parking reductions can be granted to affordable housing projects.
Council received the 2025 update, lowered the speed limit on Wideman Road between Erbsville Road and Wilmot Line to 50 km/h, and approved the matching traffic by-law amendment.
Council approved a federal grant application for a construction project and released $800,000 in 2025 capital funding for the City's share.
Council received the 2024 annual and summary drinking water reports required under provincial regulation.

debate: On 250 Lincoln Road, one delegate supported the purchase and housing but opposed demolishing the church, citing its architecture and artistic history, and asked for a cultural heritage evaluation. Another delegate urged a community centre on the site to spread services across the city.

Staff said the property is not on the heritage register and was not flagged in the heritage study. They agreed to a pre-demolition site visit by heritage staff and a heritage committee member to identify items worth salvaging. Staff also said the stained glass and art were removed or planned for removal, and the space would be filled through an expression-of-interest process.

On heritage designations, a councillor proposed removing the commercial properties from the list to allow more outreach about incentives. Another councillor worried this would create a two-part system, and one asked whether changing provincial timelines could put those properties at risk. Staff said the five owners involved supported designation in writing. Supporters said the change would not alter the City's intent and could avoid objections and tribunal appeals.

A delegate on the tariff motion asked Council to widen its procurement review to cover use of US social media platforms. Staff said they are already reviewing social media use and alternatives. The mayor said the motion did not need amending but that the concerns would be followed up.

On drinking water, councillors asked about long-term supply and growth. Staff said regional water supply strategy work is under way and that wastewater and stormwater reuse are being considered. Staff noted that water supply is not fully within City control.
